data.result:
Yes—Director review is reasonable now as an integrated development check, before committing to four shots. These stills support reviewing the look and pose direction, not approving motion; include the full clip and dust-free render when available.

Visible observations:
• Dust reads as a soft, broad cloud/haze—not obvious discrete ellipsoids—but its connection to individual hoof contacts is weak. The large beige wash behind the horse is more apparent than a grounded kick-up trail.
• Tail has a coherent taper and visible strand texture, but its silhouette remains a narrow, consolidated wedge. More strands alone would not improve that shape.
• Horse anatomy is visibly stylized/angular, especially the bulky hindquarter-to-bent-leg silhouette in the hero. The sampled poses communicate galloping intent, but do not establish convincing full-speed gallop mechanics.
• Rider’s very upright torso and forward-held arms give the selected poses a mannequin-like presentation rather than an athletic full-pace attitude. Armor contributes to that impression; actual stiffness requires playback.
• Hero framing gives the left-facing horse relatively little forward space while leaving extensive room behind for dust. The shadow is clipped at the bottom; frame 16 also crowds/crops the extended forehoof.

Next improvements, ranked:
1. Review rider/horse coupling in playback, particularly torso/hip response and the hind-leg silhouette. If it remains upright and disconnected, make a small pose adjustment—not an asset redesign.
2. Give dust a clearer near-ground contact origin and a less uniformly diffuse trailing shape; retain the soft cloud character.
3. Rebalance framing slightly for forward and lower-edge clearance while preserving enough trailing space to judge dust.

Playback must establish pace, weight, sliding, rider bounce, tail flow and dust continuity. The supplied contact metrics cannot establish those visually, and neither smoothness nor temporal failure can be inferred from these stills. Within the remaining time, targeted refinement and review are more justified than rebuilding the free assets.
